findings.summary: Nothing calls the function yet, so the real pre-Olympus queue is not actually re-triaged.
findings.evidence: `retriage` is only called from its own tests and returns decisions without appending them. The accepted reading puts wiring it into the drain or a CLI command out of scope, and the measure honestly says `status: not shown`. Making the requirement happen in operation still needs a caller that supplies the steward's still-raised keys and appends the decisions.

findings.summary: Re-triage reuses open_proposals, which skips proposals that have no brief and are above their role's limit.
findings.evidence: open_proposals keeps an item only if it has a brief or in_limit(records, w) is true (work_decisions.rs:55-59). An undecided pre-Olympus steward finding with no brief and above its role's limit is therefore never kept or closed. A filter on kind == Proposal with decision_of(...).is_none() would cover every undecided proposal.

findings.summary: `filter_map(... .ok())` silently drops any rejection error, and an id is drawn even when no decision results.
findings.evidence: rejection only fails on an empty reason, and CLOSED_REASON is a non-empty constant, so this is harmless today. If the reason ever became an input, an error would vanish without a trace.

summary: I recommend pass. OLY-A-09 in docs/spec.toml now names a real mechanism: `retriage` in crates/athena-core/src/retriage.rs. The owner is still Athena. The measure names `cargo test -p athena-core retriage` and ends with `status: not shown`. I ran the two new retriage tests, the xtask tests (which include the spec test) and the hestia tests (which include spec_gaps); all passed. Athena's recorded CI run shows fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing. If `retriage` were stubbed to keep everything, it would return nothing and the first test, which expects one decision, would fail. Changing it to ignore the still-raised keys or the Olympus cutoff would also make that test fail. Every changed file is on the expected-deliverables list. I found two minor issues. First, the function is not called from anywhere yet, so nothing re-triages the real queue; the accepted reading puts that wiring out of scope. Second, it reuses `open_proposals`, so a proposal with no brief that is above its role's limit is never looked at.
